Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "we're moving the team's 42 shared project folders from Box into SharePoint, with the copy scheduled to start after close of business friday march 14. can you put together a practical migration plan for the team, not a general explainer? include the order of work and what we tell people about where to save files. the access check has to cover all 42 folders, and the plan should say how we'll record the check and who needs to hear the outcome. if every folder passes, switch SharePoint to the primary working location on monday march 17, and keep Box available read-only through friday march 28. if even one folder doesn't pass, don't switch SharePoint to primary on march 17: keep Box as the working location and send IT the names of the folders that failed so they can resolve those access issues. don't treat a partial pass as approval to switch. we haven't picked a named owner yet, so leave that role generic. several people have bookmarked Box links, so mention what the team should know about those links without assuming they'll redirect. make the two outcomes easy to tell apart. the plan should be useful as a short internal runbook and help us prepare a team announcement, but don't draft the announcement itself. don't write as if the migration is already complete.", "output": "Prepare a practical migration plan for the team’s 42 shared project folders moving from Box to SharePoint. The copy is scheduled to start after close of business on Friday, March 14. Do not write a general explainer or imply that the migration has already been completed.

Include the order of work, where people should save files, how the access check will be recorded, and who needs to hear its outcome. The check must cover all 42 folders. Leave the owner role generic because no named owner has been chosen. Also explain what the team should know about bookmarked Box links without assuming they will redirect.

Set out these two outcomes clearly:
- If every folder passes the access check, make SharePoint the primary working location on Monday, March 17, and keep Box available as read-only through Friday, March 28.
- If even one folder fails, do not switch SharePoint to primary on March 17. Keep Box as the working location and send IT the names of the folders that failed so they can resolve the access issues. A partial pass is not approval to switch.

Make the plan useful as a short internal runbook and indicate what to cover in a team announcement, but do not draft the announcement itself."}]
